name: Neuroshima Hex: Battle - A Deep Dive into Strategic Gameplay (Opinionated Gamers)
one_line: Review/analysis of the initiative-ordered simultaneous battle resolution and Battle-token turn structure
take_what: Combat resolves in initiative tiers, highest-initiative units act first each tier and can kill lower-initiative units before those units ever act - 'you will know if they are saving one for future use' since all drawn tiles are face-up, making Battle-token bluffing a known-information mind game, not hidden info
constraint: none - mechanic not IP, only reskin needed

name: Neuroshima Hex: Battle Review (Meeple Mountain)
one_line: Reviewer's take on why the tension-then-release structure of Battle-token triggering feels like real combat
take_what: Board fills silently over many turns with zero interaction (a 'cold and calculated' placement phase) until ONE Battle tile ends the turn immediately and detonates every armed tile at once - the whole game's violence is deferred into a single player-chosen instant, not distributed turn by turn

name: Geometric Elegance: Neuroshima Hex, Now and Forever (Part I) - There Will Be Games
one_line: Design essay on faction asymmetry and how HQ placement plus limited Battle-token count force early strategic commitment
take_what: Each of 17+ factions gets only 4-6 Battle tokens total across its whole ~20-tile deck - Battle is a scarce, deck-defining resource players must ration, and faction identity is expressed through initiative-value distribution and mobility-tile count (e.g. Outpost has 7 Move tiles, Moloch has 1), not just stat totals

name: Neuroshima Hex! Wikipedia entry
one_line: Baseline rules reference: draw-3-discard-1 turn economy, 20 HQ hit points, win by HQ destruction or higher HQ total
take_what: Draw THREE tiles, discard one, play up to two per turn - the mandatory discard is a constant resource-denial choice every single turn, forcing players to burn a tile they can't use rather than stockpile a hand

name: Neuroshima Hex! Strategy blog
one_line: Player-written faction strategy guides covering the Net token and base-adjacency pressure tactics
take_what: A single 'Net' effect token can immobilize/disable an enemy HQ or key unit outright ('netting their base can totally derail' a mobility-dependent faction) - one narrow removal-of-agency card counters an entire faction archetype, creating rock-paper-scissors tension between factions rather than pure stat racing

name: Tea for Two - A Neuroshima Hex: Battle Review (Player Elimination)
one_line: Two-player-focused review discussing the swingy, cascading nature of Battle resolution once it triggers
take_what: Battle outcomes are highly variant by design - 'some battles result in a tiny firefight... others are a cascade of carnage' - because instant-action tiles (push, pull, stun) played mid-setup can chain-react through the initiative order and flip which units are even adjacent when resolution starts

name: Neuroshima Hex! armies abilities wiki (BoardGameGeek)
one_line: Community-maintained catalog of per-faction unit abilities and initiative spreads
take_what: Faction identity is legible from initiative-value distribution alone (Borgo mutants skew high-initiative/aggressive melee, Moloch skews low-initiative/heavy-armor defensive) - a player can read an opposing deck's temperament from a single stat axis without reading every card

name: Neuroshima Hex Rulebook PDF (Portal Games)
one_line: Official rulebook - primary source for the exact battle resolution algorithm and HQ shield rules
take_what: Battle resolves in strict initiative-tier passes (all tiles at initiative 3 attack simultaneously, then all surviving/undamaged tiles at initiative 2, etc.) rather than one-at-a-time - this tiered-simultaneous resolution is what lets a single Battle token detonate the whole board in one dramatic beat instead of a slow attack queue
